title: Who believed a survivor, and who didn’t? Scoring the Yekutiel fallout
summary: A San Francisco Standard political column covers fallout from the Manny Yekutiel scandal and includes a segment on District 10 supervisor candidate Theo Ellington's ambiguous stance on SFPD's Flock camera contract. Ellington voted 'no' on continuing the contract at a forum but later clarified he supports the cameras with guardrails against outside-agency access, while noting billionaire Flock proponent Chris Larsen is backing his campaign.

key_quotes.quote: "Do you support continuing SFPD's contract with Flock?" Ellington flipped his paddle to the side shaded red with an "X" on it, showing his opposition to the surveillance technology
he supports the cameras; is supportive of Lurie's latest approach, announced last week; and guardrails should stop outside agencies from accessing the data.

Ellington's bid for supervisor is propped up by a PAC that got a generous $500,000 donation from billionaire Chris Larsen — a proponent of Flock cameras. In the last two years, Larsen has committed more than $12 million toward SFPD's surveillance systems.
